title: Castellan Grid Consulting — custom software needs assessment
client: Castellan Grid Consulting, an 85-person power transmission line engineering consultancy headquartered in Denver, CO, with satellite offices in Salt Lake City, UT and Kansas City, MO. Service lines: transmission line rating studies (static/AAR/DLR), LiDAR-based vegetation management analysis (NERC FAC-003), facility ratings compliance programs (FAC-008), PLS-CADD line design & rebuild modeling, storm-hardening / resilience assessments, and inspection program support.
consultant_role: Engagement lead at Foundry Systems Advisory, hired by Castellan's COO Dana Whitfield to assess the firm's custom software needs after two blown project deadlines (Red Mesa 115kV rebuild; Sagebrush DLR study) and a near-miss FAC-008 compliance error traced to spreadsheet versioning. Produce a current-state assessment and a build/buy/configure/retain capability plan with integration architecture, phased roadmap, cost bands, and data-migration and adoption risks.

cast.name: Dana Whitfield
cast.role: COO, Castellan Grid Consulting — engagement sponsor
cast.reliability_note: Reliable on strategy, revenue, and client stakes; unreliable on technical sizing. Her '14 concurrent PLS-CADD seats' figure is a gut number with no measurement behind it (contradiction C2 trap).

cast.name: Marcus Brill
cast.role: Principal Engineer, Line Ratings — author and sole maintainer of the 2011 'RATER' Access database; retiring December 2027
cast.reliability_note: THE authoritative expert voice on rating methodology, IEEE 738 calcs, and what RATER actually does. Wrong on one thing: he believes RATER holds continuous history 'back to 2005'; the 2019 server migration destroyed pre-2013 records (C3).

cast.name: Priya Raghavan
cast.reliability_note: Accurate on inventory, licenses, and infrastructure facts. Strongly biased toward BUY for everything (champions GridVault); dismisses the compliance near-miss as 'user error' against the incident memo's systemic root cause (C7 trap).

cast.name: Kelly Nguyen
cast.role: Systems Administrator (second half of the IT team)
cast.reliability_note: Quietly authoritative on storage, backups, and the 2019 file-server migration. Her Slack posts carry the ground truth on cloud-storage volumes and the pre-2013 RATER data loss.

cast.name: Tom Okafor
cast.role: Principal Engineer, PLS-CADD Line Design practice lead
cast.reliability_note: Authoritative on PLS-CADD workflow, file-share chaos, and seat contention ('two, maybe three more seats'). Biased toward BUILD for everything — discount his 'we could write it ourselves in a summer' claims, not his facts.

cast.name: Jess Calloway
cast.reliability_note: Confidently wrong junior voice. Claims total LiDAR holdings are 'like 12 TB' (real annual intake ~38 TB), advocates moving LAS point clouds to SharePoint, and repeats GridVault's FAC-008 marketing claim as fact. Energetic, likable, must be fact-checked against Kelly/Ray/the spec.

cast.reliability_note: Reliable narrator of the two blown deadlines and the PSA distrust; she is the one who identified the three unmapped project codes that make the utilization dashboard read 61% instead of the true 68% (C5 resolution).

cast.name: Sam Trettel
cast.reliability_note: Authoritative on the compliance near-miss root cause (systemic spreadsheet versioning, not user error), audit-evidence assembly burden, and what FAC-008 workflow support actually requires.

cast.name: Ray Donnelly
cast.role: VP Engineering — Vegetation Management practice lead
cast.reliability_note: Reliable on flight volumes (1,900 line-miles/yr) and the mailed-drive workflow. Pushes a $450K in-house drone acquisition program that is out of scope for this engagement (red herring).

contradictions.topic: Traversa PSA annual cost: budget vs invoice

claim_b.quote: Traversa PSA — Annual Subscription, 70 active seats @ $70.00/seat/mo: $58,800.00

contradictions.resolution: Actual contracted cost is $58,800/yr for 70 active seats. The budget line was built on an all-staff 85-seat assumption that was never purchased.
contradictions.why_decidable: The invoice is the contractual record (dated 2025-10-01, seat count and unit price itemized) and Elena independently corroborates ('about five grand a month' = $58,800/yr ballpark); the budget CSV is a planning artifact.

contradictions.topic: PLS-CADD concurrent seats needed: COO's 14 vs licensed 9 vs true ~11

claim_a.quote: we are effectively a 14-concurrent-seat PLS-CADD shop trying to run on whatever we have

contradictions.resolution: Licensed seats = 9. The license server records only denials and queue waits (checkout_denials rising 12→41/month, 3.5-day average waits by April) — its own notes say it does not record needed seats — so concurrency must be reconstructed from the timesheet: 12 distinct PLS-CADD billers in the peak week (2026-04-10), 10–11 in other weeks. Tom Okafor asks for 'two, maybe three more seats'. True need ~11–12. Dana's 14 is an unmeasured gut figure; 9 is the constraint, not the need.
contradictions.why_decidable: The timesheet tool-tag concurrency is a measured dataset; the license report's denial/wait trend independently corroborates undersupply; the practice lead's estimate brackets the need. Only the COO memo says 14, and it cites no measurement.

claim_a.quote: RATER's got fifteen years of ratings history in it — everything back to 2011, plus the legacy runs I imported going back to 2005.

claim_b.quote: 2019 file-server migration; pre-2013 RATER records unrecoverable per restore test 2024-11

contradictions.resolution: Usable RATER history runs 2013–present (~13 years). The pre-2013 records — including all of Marcus's 2005-2011 legacy imports — were corrupted in the 2019 migration and confirmed unrecoverable by Kelly's November 2024 restore test. Migration scoping and any historical-trend features must assume a 2013 start.
contradictions.authoritative_source: sources/shared/data/tool_inventory.csv (notes field), corroborated by Kelly Nguyen in slack it-ops 2026-05-18
contradictions.why_decidable: The inventory note cites a dated restore test performed by IT; Kelly describes the corrupt-archive finding first-hand in Slack. Marcus hasn't queried the old records in years — his claim is memory of what he put in, not what survived.

claim_a.quote: Native FAC-008 facility ratings workflow — available today, out of the box.

claim_b.quote: Support confirmed the FAC-008 module is still a roadmap item — GA now targeted for Q2 2027.

contradictions.resolution: FAC-008 workflow support is not shipping; it is a roadmap item with GA targeted Q2 2027 (already slipped once, from Q4 2026). GridVault cannot be the near-term answer for the facility-ratings compliance capability; at most an 'early adopter program' bet, which is inappropriate given the near-miss.
contradictions.why_decidable: Three independent forum users report the module missing in production, one quoting a support ticket response verbatim; Grant Mosier's own follow-up email retreats to 'early adopter program' language when pressed, functionally conceding the deck overstated it.

claim_b.quote: The dashboard reads 61, but if you add back the three project codes Traversa never got mapped — 2201, 2214, 2230 — we're at 68. Nobody trusts that report and nobody should.

contradictions.resolution: True billable utilization is ~68%. Traversa PSA classifies PRJ-2201, PRJ-2214, PRJ-2230 as non-billable due to an unfixed code-mapping defect; recomputing from the raw timesheet extract with those codes billable yields 0.68.
contradictions.why_decidable: The raw timesheet extract is the system of record and the recomputation is arithmetic; the dashboard number is a derived report with a named, verifiable defect (the three codes are visibly present and billable in the extract).

contradictions.topic: LiDAR data volume: 'like 12 TB total' vs ~38 TB/yr intake

claim_a.quote: all our lidar lives in the cloud acct now, its like 12 TB total, we're fine on space

claim_b.quote: we are at 31.4 TB on that account and that is AFTER i deleted the 2023 deliveries last month to stay under quota

contradictions.resolution: Annual intake is ~38 TB (1,900 line-miles x 20 GB/mile per the acquisition spec); the account holds 31.4 TB only because older deliveries were deleted. Jess's 12 TB is wrong by 3x on stored volume and worse on intake. Storage architecture must be sized for ~38 TB/yr of new LAS data plus retention.
contradictions.why_decidable: Kelly administers the account and quotes the console number with the deletion event; the intake figure is derivable arithmetic from the flight program (Ray) and the delivery spec (GB/mile). Jess cites nothing.

contradictions.topic: Compliance near-miss root cause: user error vs systemic versioning failure

claim_a.quote: the drake thing was user error, plain and simple. someone grabbed a stale file. no software purchase fixes carelessness, a checklist does

claim_b.quote: Three versions of the Drake rating workbook existed on the project share at the time of QA; the reviewer was directed by the index sheet to a copy that had not received the March correction. No individual deviated from written procedure.

contradictions.resolution: The formal root-cause finding is systemic: uncontrolled spreadsheet versioning with a stale index, not individual carelessness. The capability plan should treat versioned, access-controlled ratings data (and eventually a computed rating engine) as the fix, not a procedure memo.
contradictions.why_decidable: The incident memo is the formal root-cause analysis signed by the compliance lead after interviews and file-share forensics; the Slack line is a hot take posted before the memo's findings and is contradicted by the memo's explicit 'no procedure deviation' finding.

contradictions.topic: GridVault per-user pricing: 'every module included' vs separately licensed LiDAR module

claim_a.quote: One simple price: $1,200 per user per year, every module included.

claim_b.quote: To your question — the LiDAR analytics module is licensed separately at $360/user/yr; it isn't part of the base bundle.

contradictions.resolution: Realistic comparable-scope year-1 cost is ~$289,200 (=$180,000 platform + 85 x $1,200 + 20 veg-practice users x $360), not the deck's implied $282,000 'all-in' — and the FAC-008 gap (C4) means even that buys less than the deck implies.
contradictions.why_decidable: The AE's written follow-up quote supersedes slide marketing copy; it is later, specific, and against the vendor's own interest — the classic tie-breaker.

red_herrings.why_distracting: Quotes the statutory maximum of $1,000,000 per violation per day and dramatic historic FAC-008/FAC-003 settlements. Tempts the agent to inflate the compliance business case with a seven-figure 'avoided penalty' number that no anchor supports; a diligent consultant uses the near-miss qualitatively and keeps quantified benefits to the $145K deadline cost and the $2.76M at-risk renewal.

A stale, abandoned 2024 ERP evaluation with three vendors and old pricing (rows dated 2024-03). Tempts scope creep into recommending a full ERP replacement; the engagement scope is engineering/delivery tooling, and the PSA finding is 'configure/remediate', not 'replace with ERP'. The 2024 prices also collide with current figures if reused.

Ray Donnelly's polished internal pitch for a $450,000 in-house drone acquisition program (aircraft, pilots, Part 107 ops). Adjacent to the LiDAR pain but it is a capex/services decision, not a software capability, and importing its $450K into the software roadmap blows the program-cost anchor.

Two-year-old plan with stale facts: 72 headcount, $16M revenue target, 'evaluate ERP in FY2025'. Plausible-looking denominators (headcount, revenue) that silently corrupt per-seat and percent-of-revenue math if used instead of the org chart and revenue CSV.

Contains Jess Calloway's confident 'move the LAS archive into SharePoint, it handles big files now' proposal (with a half-remembered 250 GB file-limit factoid). SharePoint is architecturally wrong for TB-scale point-cloud data and must not surface as a candidate product; the same thread contains Kelly's authoritative correction, rewarding careful reading.

rules: Currency: all dollar amounts in USD with '$' and comma thousands separators; amounts under $1,000,000 written in full digits (e.g., $58,800 — never '$59K'); amounts of $1,000,000+ may use the $X.XM form. Recurring costs always state the period ('/yr' or '/mo').
US English spelling throughout (per Foundry standards: 'analyze', 'organization', 'modeling').
Every numeric claim in a deliverable carries an inline source attribution in the form '(source: <document name>)'.

Gate language: no vendor may be named as a final selection before the Phase 1 validation gate. Any named candidate product must be accompanied by the exact phrase 'subject to Phase 1 validation'. The phrases 'recommendation of record' and 'final vendor selection' are prohibited in this engagement's deliverables.
The prose deliverable must close with a 'Sources Consulted' section listing the documents relied upon.
Refer to the client as 'Castellan' after first mention (never the initialism 'CGC', which collides with another Foundry client).

task.objective: Assess Castellan Grid Consulting's current tooling and workflow pain, then produce a capability plan covering what to build custom vs buy vs configure vs retain, the integration architecture, a three-phase roadmap with cost bands, and the data-migration and adoption risks — grounded strictly in the engagement source pool and compliant with Foundry's Engagement Deliverable Standards.
requirements: Establish the quantified current state: staffing, revenue at stake, current software spend, utilization, tool inventory, and the measurable costs of the two blown deadlines and the compliance near-miss.

Reconcile conflicting figures across sources before using them — at minimum the PLS-CADD seat need, the PSA subscription cost, the firm utilization rate, the LiDAR data volume, and the RATER data history span — and state which source you treated as authoritative and why.

Define 6-9 capabilities, each classified build, buy, configure, or retain, with candidate products where relevant, integration dependencies, a phase assignment, a cost band, and risk notes. The sourcing mix must reflect the evidence, not any single stakeholder's preference.
Evaluate the GridVault Suite proposal against actual requirements, explicitly testing its compliance-workflow and pricing claims against the full record.
Sequence a three-phase roadmap (Phase 1: 0-6 months; Phase 2: 6-18 months; Phase 3: 18-36 months) that respects the Palisade portal/API deadline and Marcus Brill's December 2027 retirement.
Enumerate data migrations (at minimum: RATER, the PLS-CADD file share, and the LiDAR archive) with records-at-risk and mitigation notes.
State nonfunctional requirements (versioning/auditability, security posture for hosted systems, storage scale) derived from the sources.

Comply with every rule in the Foundry Engagement Deliverable Standards (sources/engagement/kickoff/foundry_engagement_standards.md), including currency formatting, source attribution, gate language, and the closing Sources Consulted section.

deliverables.structured_schema_description: capability_plan.json must be valid JSON with exactly these top-level keys: "current_state_findings" — a list of at least 5 strings, each a quantified finding with its source document named inline; "capabilities" — a list of 6-9 objects, each with keys: "capability_id" (string, e.g. "CAP-01"), "name" (string), "pain_points_addressed" (list of strings), "build_or_buy" (exactly one of "build", "buy", "configure", "retain"), "candidate_products" (list of strings; may be empty for build), "integration_dependencies" (list of capability_ids or system names), "phase" (integer 1, 2, or 3), "est_cost_band_usd" (two-element list [lo, hi] of USD amounts), "risk_notes" (string); "roadmap" — a list of exactly 3 phase objects, each with "phase" (1|2|3), "timeline" (string, e.g. "months 0-6"), "capability_ids" (list), "exit_criteria" (string); "data_migrations" — a list of at least 3 objects, each with "migration_id" (string), "source_system" (string), "target" (string), "records_at_risk" (string), "mitigation" (string); "nonfunctional" — a list of at least 3 strings stating nonfunctional requirements.
